identity.name: Gaurav Sharma
identity.tagline: I make short films. Some of them are for [[brands]].
shortBio: I make short films — animation and documentary, most of them one to two minutes, and most of them about India.
longBio: I make short films. Most run between one and two minutes. A tiffin that comes back untouched. A thread tied every year that always fades. A boy playing a World Cup final in a backyard with a rag ball and the number 7 chalked onto it.

They tend to find the same thing from different directions: someone holding on to something small that matters more than it should. A beaver who thinks he is nothing without a crown. A man who has spent his life outrunning one fear. I am interested in the moment a person works out what they have been carrying.

Two of the films are documentary. One is about Sonam Wangchuk, who built his own school in Ladakh after the system decided he was slow. One is a tribute to a master of humane Indian modernism, an architect who held that a house is not shelter but a precious thing. Both are about people who were underestimated for a long time.

I work with generative tools. They let one person build a scene that would otherwise need a crew, a location and a budget. That is all they are to me — how the work gets made. What I care about is whether a shot holds and whether a cut lands.

processSteps.title: Work out what the film is
body: Before anything gets made, one sentence has to hold: what happens, and to whom. If it does not survive being said out loud, no amount of craft rescues it later.

processSteps.title: Find the look
body: Reference first, then a small set of rules — palette, lens, how light behaves in this world. Fixing that early is what stops a sequence drifting apart in the middle.

processSteps.title: Build the sequence
body: Shot by shot, in order, held against continuity: the same face, the same room, the same time of day. This is the slow part, and it is where most of the work goes.

processSteps.title: Cut, grade, finish
body: The edit decides the rhythm — where it breathes and where it moves. Then sound, then grade, then delivery in the format the film is actually going to be watched in.
